description: Published LOLA-derived permanently-shadowed-region (PSR) reference for the lunar south-polar Shackleton-de Gerlache region, evaluated over the exact footprint of the anchor world shackleton-de-gerlache-v1: the 151.68 km x 151.68 km lunar south-polar-stereographic square (+/-75.84 km about the pole) covered by LOLA LDEM_875S_5M.

reference.source: LOLA GDR LPSR_85S_060M_201608.IMG (PDS LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0; NASA PGDA 'Lunar Polar Illumination' product 69) - a published binary permanently-shadowed flag map at 60 m/px, 85-90S polar stereographic (R = 1737.4 km). Its PSR determination is the method of Mazarico, E., Neumann, G.A., Smith, D.E., Zuber, M.T., Torrence, M.H. (2011), 'Illumination conditions of the lunar polar regions using LOLA topography', Icarus 211, 1066-1081, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030 - horizon-based illumination over several 18.6-year lunar precession cycles.
reference.derivation: The published raster is masked to the anchor grid's footprint (|x| <= 75840 m, |y| <= 75840 m in the lunar south-polar-stereographic frame) and the flagged fraction taken: 1191354 of 6390784 cells at 60 m/px = 0.1864, i.e. 4289 km^2. The papers tabulate PSR area poleward of 80 S (16055 km^2 south, Mazarico et al. 2011; 20800 km^2 at 20 m/px, Barker et al. 2023, doi:10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1) but none tabulates this sub-region, so the reference is read directly off the published product rather than quoted second-hand.

error_budget.rationale: An ABSOLUTE budget of 5 percentage points on the permanently-shadowed area fraction. The Phase-0 model is a deliberately reduced-order one and its known approximations all bias the PSR area the same way - LOW - so the budget is sized to cover their sum, not to flatter the model. Dominant terms, in order: (1) HORIZON TRUNCATION - the horizon is searched to max_radius_m = 30 km, and no terrain outside the 151.68 km tile exists to block the Sun at all; Barker et al. (2023) compute the horizon out to 310 km using nested maps precisely because distant topography still shadows the poles. This is the largest single term and it removes shadow. (2) DEM RESOLUTION - the model runs at 120 m/px against a 60 m/px reference; the published resolution sensitivity is large and monotone (16055 km^2 at 240 m/px, Mazarico et al. 2011; 20900 km^2 at 30 m/px, O'Brien & Byrne 2022; 20800 km^2 at 20 m/px, Barker et al. 2023 - all poleward of 80 S), and coarser grids under-resolve small PSRs. (3) GRID-AZIMUTH HORIZON - RM-P0-WORLDS-03 computes the skyline in projected-grid azimuth with a grid-convergence correction rather than a rigorous per-cell topocentric one (that is RM-P1-WORLDS-12), and applies one region-centre Sun across the raster. Two terms bias the other way and are much smaller: the point-Sun approximation (no finite solar disc, worlds.md §11 open question) and the 365-day sampling window versus the 18.6-year precession cycle the published product integrates - both ADD shadow. The measured error of the committed run is 0.0400, inside the budget with margin; tightening it is what RM-P1-WORLDS-12 and a full-extent horizon radius buy.
error_budget.psr_area_fraction_note: The fraction, not the area in km^2, is the graded quantity: it is grid-independent, whereas the area depends on the cell size the mask happens to be rasterized at.

harness.note: Exactly the configuration scripts/build_shackleton_anchor.py ships the anchor world with, so the validated numbers are the numbers the published bundle carries - not a bespoke, better-tuned run. A PSR fraction is only meaningful together with the window that defines 'permanent' (PsrEpochSemantics.SEASONAL here).

notes: Reproduce with: python scripts/validate_illumination.py --terrain <anchor>/terrain --metakernel <spice>/metakernel.tm --reference validation/shackleton_psr.reference.json --report-json validation/shackleton_psr.result.json. Neither the 3.7 GB LOLA DEM nor the NAIF kernels are in the repo or in CI (which runs offline against a synthetic fixture), so the regression test that re-checks this reference is marker-gated on `realdata` and skips unless ASTRO_MINE_WORLDS_REAL_TERRAIN and ASTRO_MINE_WORLDS_METAKERNEL point at them.
